v.q: Which component receives every request in Spring MVC and delegates it?
v.w: It is the front controller. It uses handler mappings to find the controller and adapters to call it.

v.q: Which component maps a request to a controller method?
v.w: DispatcherServlet asks HandlerMapping which handler fits and then calls it through an adapter.

v.q: What is the difference between `@Controller` and `@RestController`?
o: `@RestController` adds `@ResponseBody`, so results are written as the body
`@RestController` is able to return only plain strings
`@Controller` is not able to map any URLs at all
The two annotations are completely identical in behaviour
v.w: With `@Controller` a returned String is treated as a view name. With `@RestController` it is serialised, usually as JSON.

v.q: Which statement about @RestController is NOT true?
o: It can return only plain strings
It can return objects as JSON
v.w: Return values are written to the body through message converters, so any serialisable object works.

v.q: How do you read a value from the URL path `/accounts/42`?
o: `@RequestParam` with the id after a comma
v.w: `@RequestParam` reads query strings (`?id=42`). `@RequestBody` reads and deserialises the request body.

v.q: Which annotation reads ?status=active from the URL?
v.w: @RequestParam reads query and form parameters. @PathVariable reads template segments.

v.q: What does `@Valid` on a `@RequestBody` parameter trigger?
o: Bean Validation, and an exception when a constraint fails
Encryption of the whole request body before it is read
A uniqueness check against the database for each field
Caching of the response so repeat calls are quicker
v.w: Handle the exception globally and return a `400` with field errors. Use annotations such as `@NotBlank` and `@Positive` on the DTO.

v.q: Which exception does @Valid on a @RequestBody throw on failure?
v.w: Handle it in an advice and return a 400 with the field errors.

v.q: What is the best place to translate exceptions into consistent HTTP error responses?
o: A `try/catch` block inside every controller method
The database access layer, next to the repositories
The front-end code, after the response has been received
v.w: Central handling keeps controllers clean and error bodies uniform, for example using `ProblemDetail`.

v.q: Which approach to errors is NOT recommended?
v.w: Repeated try/catch blocks lead to inconsistent responses. Centralise handling.

v.q: What is the role of a `HandlerInterceptor`?
o: Runs code before and after a controller, for concerns like logging
Parses the JSON request body into a Java object
Creates the database connections for each request
Defines the scopes that beans in the context may have
v.w: Servlet filters run earlier and see raw requests. Interceptors know the matched handler and run inside the DispatcherServlet.

v.q: Which tool runs code around every controller call, for example for timing?
v.w: An interceptor has preHandle, postHandle and afterCompletion hooks.

v.q: Which library usually converts Java objects to JSON in Spring MVC?
v.w: Content negotiation uses the `Accept` header to choose a converter. Customise Jackson with `ObjectMapper` settings or annotations.

v.q: Which statement about JSON conversion is NOT true?
o: Hibernate converts the objects to JSON
v.w: Hibernate maps entities to tables. Jackson is the JSON library.

o: Business rules belong in services, which can be tested without HTTP
Controllers are not allowed to call services
Thin controllers run faster in Tomcat
Spring forbids any logic in controllers
v.w: A controller should translate HTTP to a service call and the result back to HTTP, nothing more.

v.q: Which code belongs in a controller?
v.w: A controller adapts HTTP to the application. Rules live in services.
